chapter: Meeting Jay McShann and Martin's on the Plaza
title: Opening at Martin's on the Plaza: Gus Johnson and Pete McShann
summary: Pete McShann drummed for two weeks until Gus Johnson came from Omaha; Pete was Jay's cousin.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: So that's why when he got that job -- Walter Bills got him that job out there at Martin's on the Plaza, he had hired Gus and --
Where did Gus Johnson come from?
Well, Gus had been living in Kansas City. He had gone out to Omaha, working with bands around there.
Was he ever with Nat Towles's band?
I think he was with Red, something.
Ernie Fields, or who was the other one?
It was a Red --
Oh, Red Perkins?
Red Perkins, and what's the other band? Both these bands were out of Dallas.
Well, but he'd come back to Kansas City by that --
No, what's his name asked him to join them, so he had to give them two week's notice. That's why Pete McShann and I opened with McShann's at Martin's on the Plaza.
Well, now, Pete McShann, how long did he stay with the group?
Until Gus got there in two weeks, you know.
Was Pete younger than Jay, or --
They're about the same age. Yeah, cousins, first cousins, you know.
Well, now, was he a good drummer? Did he stay in music?

He stayed there for quite a while. I'd say until maybe 1941, '42. He married and his wife made him get out of it. But after they separated he married again, and he had a band up until a few years ago when the doctor told him he should take it easy, or something.
He kept the band?
Well, you know, little gig bands, you know.
Oh, I see.
Nothing like big bands.
Oh, I think somewhere -- I believe in this book they say Pete McShann was Jay's brother.
No, he's a first cousin.
Oh, yeah, that's right. It's got, his cousin, Pete McShann.
